header.title: How to Replace a Circuit Breaker Fuse
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to safely replace a circuit breaker fuse. Follow these steps to identify, remove, and install a new fuse with the correct amperage.

steps.description: This step involves opening the fuse box by removing the cover and switching off the main electricity switch.
actions: Wear rubber-soled shoes
Ensure the floor beneath the circuit breaker box is dry
Remove the circuit breaker box cover
Unscrew the corners with a screwdriver
Push the main electricity switch to the 'off' position

steps.description: Inspect fuses to identify the type of problem based on their condition.
actions: Inspect the push-lever of frequently tripping fuses.
Check if circuit breaker fuses are off and cannot be reset.
Examine fuses that refuse to trip for signs of overheating or damage.

steps.description: Check for voltage across the faulty fuse using a multimeter.
actions: Turn the damaged fuse off if it’s not already
Set your multimeter to "Volt AC"
Rest one pin on the terminal screw of the faulty fuse
Rest the other pin on the ground screw
Observe the reading on the multimeter
Do not continue if voltage is indicated

steps.description: This step details how to remove a circuit breaker fuse by either unscrewing or pulling it from its socket, ensuring wire connections are detached and noting the wire colors.
actions: Unscrew the fuse
Pull or lever the fuse from its socket
Detach wires from the fuse
Loosen the terminal screws
Note which color wire attaches to which end of the fuse

steps.description: Ensure the replacement fuse has the same amperage and voltage as the original fuse.
actions: check fuse amperage
take old fuse to store
purchase correct replacement

steps.description: This step involves setting a new fuse to the 'off' position, connecting the wires, and inserting it into its socket.
actions: Set the new fuse to the "off" position.
Insert the original wires, in turn, into the terminals of the new fuse.
Tighten the retaining screws with a screwdriver.
Push the new fuse back into its socket.
Tighten screws after inserting them (if supplied).

steps.description: Reconnect the power supply by turning on the circuit breaker and securing the box cover with screws.
actions: Switch the circuit breaker fuse box back on
Replace the box cover
Insert the screws
Tighten them
